recognize_zh: 周邊血中許多紅血球的中央淡染區呈細長裂縫狀（箭頭），像嘴巴一樣，這就是口形紅血球（stomatocyte）；視野中另有兩顆嗜中性球與一顆偏大的多染性紅血球。
features: Numerous red cells with slit-like, mouth-shaped central pallor (stomatocytes, arrow)
Stomatocytes distributed across the field rather than only in thick areas
Occasional larger polychromatophilic red cell (upper right)
Two neutrophils, one with a band-like nucleus; a partial lymphocyte at lower left
No spherocytes, target cells or red cell fragments prominent
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous red cells with slit-like central pallor (stomatocytes, arrow) distributed evenly across a well-spread area of the smear. An occasional larger polychromatophilic red cell is noted. Leukocytes, including two neutrophils, appear unremarkable. Findings are consistent with stomatocytosis; if artifact is excluded, differential considerations include hereditary stomatocytosis, liver disease with alcohol use, and Rh-null phenotype.

ddx.vs: Artifactual stomatocytes appear only in thick areas of the smear and disappear in well-spread areas or wet preparations, whereas true stomatocytes are present throughout.
Spherocytes are small dense cells lacking central pallor, while stomatocytes retain a slit-like pallor; osmotic fragility and EMA binding help separate them.
SAO shows oval cells with one or two transverse bars or slits (theta cells), and is caused by a SLC4A1 deletion.
Morphology is similar; clinical history and absence of family history distinguish acquired from hereditary forms.
